result.prompt: A portrait-format 2:3 open mic gig poster in electric yellow and deep charcoal, viewed straight-on with crisp, flat graphic lighting and no perspective distortion. A huge illustrated vintage microphone dominates the lower-right two-thirds, tilted diagonally upward toward the center, its rounded charcoal grille built from thick yellow slits and its handle rendered with bold angular shadows. Irregular concentric sound-wave arcs burst behind it, forming an energetic yellow-and-charcoal rhythm that frames the lettering without crossing it. Across the upper half, the only text reads exactly “Open Mic Night · Friday 7pm · The Blue Door”, arranged as a cohesive three-line lockup with line breaks after each middle dot. “Open Mic Night” uses oversized, expressive condensed display lettering with slightly uneven baselines; “Friday 7pm” and “The Blue Door” use smaller, clear condensed sans-serif lettering, with both separator dots clearly visible. Generous charcoal negative space gives the yellow lettering impact. Rough screen-printed edges, subtle ink misregistration, and fine paper grain lend tactile gig-poster character, while strong silhouettes and disciplined spacing keep everything readable.
